name: Nebius Group
day_summary: SATURDAY WEEKEND REVIEW — US MARKETS CLOSED; $240.30 LAST CLOSE (JUNE 26, −6.36%); HIGH-BETA NEOCLOUD HIT IN A RISK-OFF TAPE. No US equity trading June 27 (Saturday). NBIS last traded at $240.30 (June 26, −$16.33, −6.36% from $256.63). This is what a high-beta AI-infrastructure name does on a risk-off day: it falls harder than the index (SPX 7,354, below the 7,460 floor; VIX ~18.41) and harder than the compute bellwether (NVDA −2.20%), in line with the broader AI-capex de-risking that hit the whole complex (SK Hynix −8.36% on KOSPI circuit breakers, Micron −6.69%). Nothing company-specific broke — the ~$47B backlog (Microsoft, Meta) and the neocloud demand story are intact — but Nebius is the public proxy for the compute-and-power bottleneck, and when the market de-risks the AI-capex trade, the highest-beta expression of it gets sold first. Day winner: BEARS — the risk-off tape did the damage; this is a beta event, not a thesis event.
long_pnl: longs gave back −6.36% on June 26 in a broad AI de-risking; the name is still a multiple of its 52-week low ($43.89) and the ~$47B backlog underwrites years of revenue, but at this size in this tape the position is a hold-small, don't-press trade; the cleanest read is that NBIS will trade with the AI-capex risk appetite (NVDA, CRWV, the power names) more than on any Nebius-specific news until the next print
short_pnl: bears riding the 'high beta + capex/dilution overhang' thesis had a clean session: −6.36% on a risk-off day with no company catalyst is exactly the playbook — high-beta neoclouds fall first and fastest when the AI-capex trade de-risks; the structural short risk is that the same beta cuts the other way violently on any risk-on reversal (an NVDA stop reset June 29, a strong neocloud print), so this is a tactical win, not a position to overstay

decision.horizon: 2–4 quarters · into the next quarterly print and the AI-capex cycle
decision.rationale: HOLD at LOW conviction — own it small, don't press it here. The bull case is real: Nebius is a pure-play on the compute-and-power bottleneck that the whole Situational Awareness thesis is built around, with a ~$47B backlog from Microsoft and Meta that gives multi-year revenue visibility few names can match. But two things keep conviction low: (1) it is a high-beta vehicle — a −6.36% day on no company news shows it trades as a leveraged bet on AI-capex risk appetite, so position size, not entry price, is the main risk control; (2) the funding question is unresolved — the $20–25B FY26 capex plan implies meaningful debt and/or equity dilution, and how that's financed is the swing factor on the equity. Into a hostile macro week (regime gates breached, NFP July 2 into the July 3 close), the right posture is hold a small position and let the next print — and any Aschenbrenner 13F move (next filing ~Aug 14) — tell you whether to upgrade. Sibling CRWV (also a disclosed Aschenbrenner long) is the cleanest read-across; the neocloud complex trades together.

analysis: Nebius did on June 26 exactly what a high-beta AI-infrastructure name does in a risk-off tape: it fell −6.36%, harder than the index and harder than NVDA, with no company-specific news. That is the most important thing to internalize about owning it — NBIS is a leveraged call option on AI-capex risk appetite, so position size is the risk control, not entry price. The bull case is genuinely strong: a ~$47B backlog from Microsoft and Meta is multi-year revenue visibility, and Nebius is the cleanest public proxy for the compute-and-power bottleneck the Situational Awareness page is built around. The two things that keep conviction low are funding (the $20–25B FY26 capex must be financed without crippling dilution) and beta into a hostile week (regime gates breached, NFP July 2 into the July 3 close). Hold it small, watch the sibling CRWV and the next Aschenbrenner 13F (~Aug 14) for confirmation, and let the funding picture and the next print decide whether to upgrade.

so_what.line: If you hold Nebius, hold it small and don't add here — Friday's −6.4% was the high-beta tax of owning a leveraged AI-capex bet on a risk-off day, not a crack in the $47B-backlog story; let size, not timing, be your risk control into a hostile macro week.
